quote: The MBR treatment process is highly data-driven and requires continuous monitoring. Operators must be proactive, careful and diligent—MBRs aren’t as forgiving as a conventional activated sludge process. It’s a chemical process more than a biological process. Cleaning the membranes properly is key, as is managing the aeration system. Once the membranes get fouled, they can’t be recovered quickly. The team’s ability to work with instrumentation and small mechanical components is important. Proper training is essential. Jacobs’ membrane technologists are really good—we pull them in all the time for advice or send them data to review. The membrane manufacturer will always point fingers elsewhere, so it’s great to have someone who can read the data and spot trends to help solve a problem.
speaker: Anthony Benavidez

quote: With my ability to lead and motivate teams, and unwavering commitment to excellence, I am ready to serve as the Operations (& Compliance) Manager for the County. I am dedicated to continuous improvements ensuring that I will drive your operations to new heights. I plan to be instrumental in achieving your goals and fostering a culture of success.
speaker: Devon Trezevant

quote: As a manager, I like to keep an open door policy. I want my direct reports and anyone else on the team to feel comfortable coming to me with anything, whether it be a concern, suggestion, or just to talk. My team is a second family and I always want to be there for them. When it comes to training, I believe if people are invested they can learn all aspects of maintenance. I don’t micromanage because everyone learns differently and at their own pace. People see things through different sets of eyes and I learn from my team just as much as I hope they learn from me.
speaker: Nathan Dahl
